prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- “Real change” to rebalance wealth and power, end austerity, and tackle the climate emergency while raising living standards.

Economy, investment and ownership
- £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund) plus a National Investment Bank with £250bn lending; regional banks and local transformation funds.
- Rewriting Treasury rules to align all investment with climate goals; crackdown on tax avoidance; higher income tax only for those earning over £80,000; partial reversal of corporation tax cuts; no rises in VAT, NI or income tax for others.
- Bring rail, mail, water and energy into public ownership; free full‑fibre broadband nationwide by 2030 via “British Broadband.”
- Worker voice: one‑third of company boards elected by workers; Inclusive Ownership Funds (up to 10% employee stake).

Green Industrial Revolution
- Aim for substantial majority of emissions cuts by 2030; net‑zero energy system in the 2030s.
- 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low‑carbon by 2030; 7,000 offshore and 2,000 onshore wind turbines, major solar build‑out; new nuclear; ban fracking; expand storage and grid; trial tidal; scale hydrogen.
- Upgrade almost all 27m homes; zero‑carbon standard for new homes; windfall tax on oil firms.
- 1 million climate jobs; Climate Apprenticeships; R&D to 3% of GDP.

Transport
- Rail and buses back to public control; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils run services; restore cut routes.
- Complete HS2 to Scotland; Crossrail for the North; national electrification; more rail freight, cycling and walking.
- End new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; invest in EV charging and zero‑emission public fleets.

NHS and care
- Average 4.3% annual NHS funding rise; end and reverse privatisation; abolish prescription charges; free annual dental check‑ups; invest in diagnostics/IT.
- Mental health parity, 24/7 crisis care, modernised estates.
- National Care Service with free personal care; stronger home support; better pay and conditions for care workers.

Education
- National Education Service: free lifelong learning; abolish university tuition fees; restore maintenance grants and EMA.
- 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; restore/expand Sure Start.
- More school funding; class sizes max 30 in primary; scrap SATs; Arts Pupil Premium; bring academies/free schools into local democratic control.

Work, rights and pay
- Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all aged 16+; ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral collective bargaining; stronger union rights.
- Target 32‑hour average full‑time week within a decade with no loss of pay.
- Cap overdraft/loan charges; tackle late payments to SMEs/self‑employed.

Housing
- Build over 1 million council/social homes in a decade (at least 150k a year; 100k council homes); end Right to Buy; redefine “affordable” by incomes.
- Private renting: rent controls linked to inflation with local powers to go further; open‑ended tenancies; national licensing; renters’ unions.
- Grenfell response: £1bn for sprinklers and fire safety; remove dangerous cladding.
- End rough sleeping within five years.

Security, justice and communities
- Rebuild neighbourhood policing; more officers/PCSOs; youth services restored.
- Probation reunified publicly; restore early legal aid; presumption against <6‑month sentences for non‑violent offences.
- Strengthen victims’ rights; tackle VAWG (commissioner, refuge funding, decriminalise abortion).

Migration and equality
- End the “hostile environment”; scrap 2014 Immigration Act; end indefinite detention; close Yarl’s Wood/Brook House; right to work for refugees.
- Automatic right to stay for EU citizens.
- New Department for Women and Equalities; enforce equal pay; extend pay‑gap reporting (gender, BAME, disability); stronger disability and LGBT+ rights.

Brexit
- Final‑say referendum within six months: remain vs a new deal (UK‑wide customs union, close single market alignment, rights and standards protections). Implement outcome; rule out no‑deal.

Constitution and democracy
- Abolish House of Lords for an elected Senate (via constitutional convention); votes at 16; automatic voter registration; tougher lobbying rules; curb second jobs for MPs; extend FOI.

International and defence
- Human‑rights‑led foreign policy; War Powers Act; suspend arms sales used in rights abuses (e.g., Yemen); recognise State of Palestine.
- Lead on climate diplomacy; maintain NATO, spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; renew Trident; improve forces’ pay, housing and veterans’ support.

Social security and pensions
- Scrap Universal Credit; emergency reforms: end five‑week wait and sanctions; scrap benefit cap/two‑child limit; raise LHA; split/fortnightly payments.
- Maintain triple lock; keep state pension age at 66; address 1950s women’s pension injustice (with co‑designed recompense).
